functions.get_customer(customer_id: str): returns Customer(id, name, discount, region) or None; discount is fraction (10 -> 0.10); region is str e.g. "TX"

functions.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct): lines: iterable of (category str, amount_cents int) pairs. region: str such as TX, or None for an unknown customer (tax 0). discount_pct: percent number (10 means 10 percent). Returns total tax in integer cents, rounded half up. Raises KeyError if region is a str not in rates.csv.
functions.tax_rate_pct(region) -> Decimal: percent number for region, e.g. Decimal(8.25). Raises KeyError if region not found.
functions.is_exempt(category) -> bool: True if category is listed in exempt_categories.csv.

value.notes: invoice.py passes customer.region and customer.discount (percent number, per team standard) plus the (category, amount_cents) of each line. tax.py applies the exemption and discount itself. tax.py does not look up items or customers.

pricing.py.is_known_sku(sku) -> bool: True if the SKU exists in pricing data
pricing.py.unit_price(sku) -> Decimal: Decimal dollars; Decimal("0") if SKU unknown
pricing.py.customer_name(customer_id) -> str: Name; "" if unknown (invoice falls back to the id)
pricing.py.discount_multiplier(customer_id) -> Deci: 10% off = Decimal("0.90"); unknown customer = Decimal("1") (no discount; 0 would mean 100% off)

tax.py.tax_for(customer_id, lines, discount) ->: lines = list of (sku, Decimal line_amount) for KNOWN skus only, in order; discount = Decimal dollars already computed by invoice. tax.py owns all taxability rules (which lines/base are taxed). tax_amount rounded to cent, half-up. tax_multiplier e.g. Decimal("1.0825") for 8.25%; unknown customer or no tax -> (Decimal("0.00"), Decimal("1"))

value.invoice.py: render_invoice(order) only computes subtotal, discount = (subtotal * (1 - discount_multiplier)) quantized to cent half-up, total; and formats percents as (multiplier-1)*100 without trailing zeros.
